summary: Sustained 5xx following autoscaler liveness probe restart loop and API gateway queueing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (CloudScale AI, Dedicated) reported sustained elevated 5xx rates for text-generation and streaming calls beginning ~2026-03-10T11:45Z. Errors were predominantly 502/503 from the API gateway with upstream runtime exits and OOM-style messages in runtime logs.

Impact:
- Broad error rate increase for one tenant in us-east-1; customer reported failed requests for multi-tenant endpoints and degraded throughput for pinned model versions.
- Client-facing latency increased and streaming sessions frequently terminated mid-response.

Observed environment:
- prod | us-east-1, dedicated cluster assigned to CloudScale AI.
- Autoscaler recently had a canary change deployed (service autoscaler backoff/refactor) ~2026-03-09 22:00Z.

Initial runtime logs / metrics snippet:
- api-gateway: 502/503 spike from 11:44-13:10, concurrent connections queued > connection_pool_size for several proxies
- serving-runtime: repeated process exits with stack traces referencing memory allocation failures and kernel fallback logs (jit-kernel swap)
- autoscaler: series of small-scale ups and immediate downs, liveness probe failures clustered at 11:40-11:50

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send steady stream of requests at customer traffic shape (mixed short/long sequences with streaming enabled).
2) Autoscaler performs a transient scale-up; new pods fail liveness and restart quickly in sequence.
3) API gateway connection queue grows; gateway returns 502/503 while retry amplification increases upstream load.

Supporting links and dashboards:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/rtx/errors?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T11:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T13:30:00Z
- Logs (SPL): https://logs.redwood/search?q=INC-2026-03-10-12
- Slack thread: #support /thread/CK12AB34 (see transcript)
steps_to_reproduce: Use customer traffic replay (tenant: cloudscale-ai) from 2026-03-09 to reproduce. Observe autoscaler scale events, liveness probe failures, and api-gateway 502s when request concurrency ramps beyond connection_pool_size.
logs_snippets:
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:49:23Z ERROR: runtime exited with code 137; allocator: failed reserve; kernel-fallback: true
[autoscaler] 2026-03-10T11:48:57Z WARN: liveness probe failed: health-check timeout (0.9s)
[api-gateway] 2026-03-10T11:50:01Z WARN: upstream conn queue full -> returning 503
investigation_notes: 11:46 - initial customer alert received; SPoC created.
11:50 - on-call SRE observed repeated small restarts on serving-runtime pods for the tenant; liveness probe failures coincident with restarts.

11:55 - hypothesis A: autoscaler canary change introduced aggressive probe/config that caused pod churn at scale-up and left runtimes cold (kernel fallback), increasing memory pressure and causing OOM-like exits.
12:05 - hypothesis B: API gateway retry/backoff not compensating for rapidly restarting upstreams, causing connection queue amplification and 5xx responses upstream.

12:20 - validated with logs: runtime exits (137) + kernel fallback logs after a recent batching kernel selection change (PR referenced). PR 5182 introduced a background prefetch change to batching that increased memory fragmentation under certain sequence-length distributions.
12:30 - reproduced locally with a scaled-down tenant replay; toggling the canary autoscaler config to previous backoff removed the restart loop.
12:45 - mitigation executed: rolled back autoscaler canary, routed tenant traffic to a warm fallback model variant (opt-6.7b-q4) with reserved capacity, and increased gateway queue depth temporarily.
13:00 - error rates decreased to baseline; customer confirmed recovery for most requests by 13:10.

Investigation concluded that the root cause was a combination of three factors: recent autoscaler liveness timing change + a batching kernel change that under cold-starts increased memory pressure + API gateway retry amplification during rapid upstream churn.

resolution:
Root cause: interaction between an autoscaler liveness/probe config change (canary) and a recent batching/kernel selection change that increased memory fragmentation on cold-starts. The autoscaler change caused rapid restart loops which amplified API gateway retries, creating connection queue saturation and widespread 502/503 responses.

Fixes applied:
- Immediate rollback of the autoscaler canary (2026-03-10 12:20Z).
- Traffic rerouted for customer to reserved fallback pool for warm capacity.
- Reverted the problematic batching prefetch change in runtime (revert PR 5190) and queued a safer rollout with additional memory tests.
- Tweaked API gateway retry settings and temporarily increased connection pool depth to reduce early 5xx while recovery proceeded.

Status: Full customer recovery confirmed by 2026-03-10T13:20Z. Incident marked resolved after monitoring window.
follow_up_actions: Postmortem scheduled: draft at https://confluence.redwood/internal/incidents/autoscaler-liveness-loop (owner: Diego Ramos).
Add autoscaler backoff jitter and increase liveness timeout for warm-start shapes (owner: Platform Eng).
Add pre-merge memory-fragmentation regression tests for batching kernel changes (owner: Runtime team).
Update runbook: include step to route impacted tenant to reserved fallback pool before rollback to reduce customer impact.
Monitor: 72-hour elevated monitoring for similar patterns across dedicated tenants.
